en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Confession (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Ovādavagga 27.
The Training Rule on Arrangements.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, having made an appointment with the bhikkhunīs, set out on a journey along the same road.
People criticized, grumbled, and complained, saying:
"Just as we wander about with our wives, so too do these recluses, sons of the Sakyans, wander about having made an appointment with the bhikkhunīs."
The monks heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those monks who were few in desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the group-of-six monks, having made an appointment with bhikkhunīs, set out on a journey along the same road?"... [and so on].
“Is it true, monks, that you set out on a journey together with the bhikkhunīs by appointment?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, you foolish men, can you set out on a journey together with bhikkhunīs after making an appointment?
This, foolish men, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“Whatever bhikkhu, having made an appointment with a bhikkhunī, should set out on a journey along a highway, even if only as far as the next village, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Thus was this training rule laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.
Now at that time, a number of bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs were traveling along a highway from Sāketa to Sāvatthī.
Then those bhikkhunīs said this to those bhikkhus:
“We too will go along with you, venerable sirs.
“Sisters, it is not permissible for one to set out on a journey along a highway in company with a bhikkhunī after making an appointment.”
“Either you go first, or we shall go.
“Venerable sir, the masters are the foremost persons;
let the masters go first.”
Then, as those bhikkhunīs were traveling along, robbers plundered them and violated them on the way.
Having reached Sāvatthī, those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs,
and the bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus.
The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma with reference to this cause and this occasion, addressed the monks:
“I allow you, monks, when traveling on a road that is considered dangerous and fearful, to set out on the same journey together with a nun after making an appointment.”
And so, monks, you should recite this training rule:

“Whichever monk, having made an appointment with a nun, should travel along a highway together with her, even if only as far as the next village, except at the proper time, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Herein, this is the proper time: when the road is one that must be traveled by caravan and is considered dangerous and fearful—this is the proper time therein.”
"But whoever" means whoever such [a person]... "a bhikkhu" means... [as before].
... [as before] ... this is the meaning intended here by "bhikkhu.
A "bhikkhunī" is one who has received full ordination in both Saṅghas.
"Saddhiṃ" means together.
"Saṃvidhāya" means—

If she makes an appointment, saying, “Let us go, sister,” “Let us go, noble brother,” “Noble brother, let us go,” “Sister, let us go,” or “Let us go today, or yesterday, or tomorrow,” there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
“Even as far as the interval between villages” means:
in a village where a cock can fly, for every interval between villages, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
In a forest that is devoid of a village, at every half-yojana, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Except on an occasion" means setting aside the occasion.
A "road requiring a caravan" is one that cannot be traveled without a caravan.
A "perilous" road...
On that road, the place where the robbers have encamped is seen; the place where they have eaten is seen; the place where they have stood is seen; the place where they have sat is seen;

the place where they have lain down is seen. That road is indeed dangerous: men are seen there who have been killed by the robbers, seen who have been plundered, and seen who have been beaten. Having traveled along that dangerous road, one should show it to be safe and dismiss them, saying: "Go, sisters."

If one has made an appointment and perceives that an appointment has been made, and one sets out on a journey along the same road—even if only as far as the next village—except at the appropriate time, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

If one has made an appointment but is unsure of it, and one sets out on a journey along the same road—even if only as far as the next village—except at the appropriate time, there is an offense of expiation.

If one has made an appointment but does not perceive that an appointment has been made, and one sets out on a journey along the same road—even if only as far as the next village—except at the appropriate time, there is an offense of expiation.
If the monk makes an appointment and the nun does not, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she has not made an appointment, yet he perceives that she has, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she has not made an appointment, yet he is in doubt about it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it has not been stored and he perceives that it has not been stored, there is no offense.
There is no offense at the proper time.
She goes without having made an appointment;
the bhikkhunī makes an appointment, while the bhikkhu does not;
they go by means of a different signal.
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for an original offender.
The seventh training rule concerning arrangements is finished.
